questions.q: What is the capstone project built across Lessons 29-31?
options: A production RAG knowledge assistant over a single, real knowledge base
A new embedding model trained from scratch
A general-purpose chatbot with no retrieval component
A vector database engine built from first principles
questions.explain: The capstone is scoped to one real knowledge base so every pipeline stage from the course has an actual, working job to do.

questions.q: Why is the capstone deliberately scoped to one knowledge base instead of several?
options: Vector databases cannot store more than one collection
To demonstrate that every pipeline stage is actually working end to end, rather than spreading effort thin across multiple half-finished sources
Because embedding models can only process one document at a time
Because re-ranking only works on a single source
questions.explain: A single knowledge base done completely — with real ingestion, retrieval, re-ranking, citations, and failure handling — demonstrates more than multiple sources with those stages only partially working.

questions.q: According to the kickoff checklist, what must the abstention path do to count as 'done'?
options: Fire based on a real score_threshold when retrieval confidence is low
Always return a fabricated best-guess answer
Only apply to questions longer than 50 words
Replace the re-ranking step entirely
questions.explain: The done checklist specifically calls for a score_threshold abstention path — a mechanical way to recognize low-confidence retrieval and respond honestly, from Lesson 22.

questions.q: Which chapter does this lesson map directly onto the evaluation and tuning work in Lesson 30?
options: Chapter 1 (Why RAG Exists)
Chapter 2 (Embeddings Deep Dive)
Chapter 3 (Vector Databases)
Chapter 5 (Advanced RAG Patterns)
questions.explain: Chapter 5 covered the evaluation metrics (context precision/recall, faithfulness, answer relevancy) that Lesson 30's tuning pass is built directly from.

questions.q: What does this lesson say about whether the capstone introduces any new concepts?
options: It introduces three entirely new frameworks not covered earlier in the course
It requires learning a new programming language
It introduces nothing new — every piece is a direct application of something already covered in Lessons 1 through 27
It only covers concepts from Chapter 6 itself
questions.explain: The capstone is explicitly framed as application, not new learning — every build step maps back to a specific earlier chapter's content.
